g.text: Script heterogeneity: a concrete source of silent failures
In practice, ya and kaf code points differ across Persian, Pashto and Dari text, so string matching, deduplication
and tokenization break without any error message. (Code points shown here as an illustration.)
About a dozen scripts across the family, most only historical. Living varieties use Perso-Arabic, Latin and
Cyrillic, often in parallel; Tajik uses Cyrillic only. Priority: one shared Iranic normalization library.
Normalize before you train, or related varieties look unrelated.
